newsitem.title: USA: Berkshire Gas sets $16 mln refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire Gas sets $16 mln refinancing.

text.p: Berkshire Gas Co will close this week on the refinancing of $16 million of debt and equity which both lowers its cost of money and provides tax benefits, Chief Financial Officer Michael J. Marrone said on Wednesday.

He told the annual meeting that First Colony Corp has agreed to purchase a senior note "at a rate of 7.8 percent allowing us to retire the 8.4 percent preferred stock series and refinance the 9-1/9 percent debentures and two small first mortgage bonds.
"The aggregate benefit to the bottom line of both the savings in borrowing costs and the tax benefits totals $288,000 annually, or the equivalent of $0.135 per share," Marrone said.

He also said the company's dividend reinvestment program is being changed to increase the limits on cash contributions in addition to the dividend to $5,000 per quarter from $3,000 eligible for the 3 percent discount on stock purchases through the plan.
Also, he said, share owners whose stock is held in street name are now also eligible to have their dividends reinvested.

Noting fiscal 1996's record sales of eight billion cubic feet of natural gas, chief executive Scott S. Robinson said the company continues to see strong growth in demand for natural gas and propane despite a shrinking population base as small businesses grow to fill the void created by larger employers.

"When you realize that we sold more gas last year than we did when GE employed 10,000 plus people in Pittsfield alone, it becomes clear that the diversification of our area economy has more than made up for manufacturing losses."
